questions.question: Explain the difference between a subscript and a coefficient, using 2H2O as the example, and state which may be changed when balancing.
questions.expected_answer: In 2H2O the subscript 2 (after H) shows that each water molecule contains two hydrogen atoms; it is part of the formula and fixed by the identity of the substance. The coefficient 2 (in front) shows that there are two water molecules. Only coefficients may be changed when balancing, because changing a subscript would change the substance.

questions.question: Use a table to show whether CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O is balanced.
questions.expected_answer: Carbon: left 1, right 1. Hydrogen: left 4, right 2 × 2 = 4. Oxygen: left 2 × 2 = 4, right 2 + 2 = 4. All elements match, so the equation is balanced.

questions.question: State the law of conservation of mass and explain why magnesium ribbon appears to gain mass when burnt in an open crucible.
questions.expected_answer: In a closed system the total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants, because atoms are rearranged but not created or destroyed. In an open crucible, oxygen from the air (not weighed at the start) combines with the magnesium to form magnesium oxide, so the product weighs more than the magnesium alone; if the oxygen used is included, mass is conserved.
